title: Detecting SnRK2 Kinase Activity in Plants by Immunoblotting and In-Gel Assay
author: Li, Yuan, et al.
materials: This step applies to all four methods. It describes details that might influence the experimental results, including the sowing density and the duration of vernalization.1.Sterilize the seeds using 5% sodium hypochlorite for 12 min in a 1.5 mL tube.2.Wash the seeds four times with double-distilled water on a clean bench.3.Plant the seeds evenly in a 10 cm × 10 cm square Petri dish that contains solid 1/2 MS, 1% sucrose, and 1.2% agar, pH 5.7–5.8 (Figure 1A).Figure 1Sample preparation, stress treatment, and sample collection(A) Approximately 75 seeds are dotted uniformly onto the solid 1/2 MS medium. Scale bar: 2 cm.(B) Petri dishes are positioned upright with proper spacing in the incubator.(C) 9-day-old seedlings are used to evaluate SnRK2 activity in vivo. Scale bars: 2 cm (left) or 0.5 cm (right).(D) Gently transfer the seedlings to a six-well plate containing the liquid 1/2 MS medium and submerge them entirely for a two-hour pre-treatment.(E) Gently transfer the seedlings into the 1/2 liquid MS medium without or with ABA or mannitol, and incubate them for the indicated times.(F) Carefully remove the residual liquid medium from the seedlings with tissue paper after the treatments.(G) Protein extraction buffer is directly applied to seedlings to prevent ice immobilization of steel balls.4.Seal the plates using micropore tape and stratify the seeds at 4°C for 48 h in the dark.5.Grow the seedlings vertically in a Percival CU36L5 incubator at 22°C for 7 days under a 16-hour light and 8-hour dark photoperiod (Figures 1B and 1C).CRITICAL: The seed planting density should be fixed to ensure the repeatability of the results. Typically, 75 seeds can be grown in three rows per Petri dish (Figure 1A). The intensity of light also affects SnRK2 activity. Therefore, the plant material prepared for the same experiment should be placed in the same location within the incubator, with a light intensity of 56–87.5 μmol m−2 s−1. Under high light conditions, cotyledons accumulate anthocyanin and are unsuitable for assessing SnRK2 activity.

This step applies to immunoblotting with anti-phospho-S175-SnRK2s antibody, in-gel kinase assay, and band shift assay. steps.title: Prepare plant seedlings
steps.instruction: Sterilize seeds in 5 % sodium hypochlorite for 12 min in a 1.5 mL tube, wash four times with double‑distilled water, and sow ~75 seeds uniformly on a 10 cm × 10 cm square Petri dish containing solid ½ MS, 1 % sucrose, 1.2 % agar (pH 5.7–5.8). Seal with micropore tape, stratify at 4 °C in darkness for 48 h, then grow vertically in a Percival CU36L5 incubator at 22 °C under a 16 h light/8 h dark cycle (light intensity 56–87.5 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹) for 7 days.

substeps.instruction: Sterilize seeds in 5 % NaOCl for 12 min (1.5 mL tube).
Wash seeds 4× with double‑distilled water on a clean bench.
Plate ~75 seeds evenly on ½ MS + 1 % sucrose + 1.2 % agar (pH 5.7–5.8) in a 10 cm × 10 cm dish.
Seal with micropore tape and stratify at 4 °C, dark, 48 h.
Grow vertically at 22 °C, 16 h light/8 h dark, light intensity 56–87.5 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ for 7 days.

steps.title: Stress‑treat seedlings
steps.instruction: Transfer 9‑day‑old seedlings to a six‑well plate containing liquid ½ MS medium and submerge for a 2‑h pre‑treatment; then move seedlings to liquid ½ MS with or without ABA or mannitol and incubate for the indicated times; finally remove residual liquid with tissue paper and apply protein‑extraction buffer directly to the seedlings.

substeps.instruction: Gently transfer seedlings to six‑well plate with liquid ½ MS; submerge for 2 h.
Transfer seedlings to liquid ½ MS containing either no additive, ABA, or mannitol; incubate for the experimental time points.
Remove remaining liquid using tissue paper.
Apply protein‑extraction buffer directly to seedlings.

steps.title: Extract total protein
steps.instruction: Grind frozen seedlings on ice with an automatic grinder, vortex, keep on ice 10 min, centrifuge at 20 000 × g for 40 min at 4 °C, transfer supernatant, determine protein concentration with Bradford assay, mix 80 µg protein with 4× SDS loading buffer to 40 µL, and boil at 98 °C for 3 min.

substeps.instruction: Grind samples into powder on ice using an automatic grinding machine.
Vortex thoroughly; incubate on ice 10 min.
Centrifuge 20 000 × g, 40 min, 4 °C.
Transfer supernatant to a new 1.5 mL tube.
Add 3 µL supernatant to 600 µL 1× Bradford reagent; measure concentration with BioPhotometer Plus.
Combine 80 µg total protein with 4× SDS loading buffer to a final volume of 40 µL.
Boil at 98 °C for 3 min (samples can be stored at –80 °C after rapid LN₂ freezing).

steps.title: Run SDS‑PAGE and transfer
steps.instruction: Prepare a 10 % SDS‑PAGE gel (1.0 mm thick, 15 wells) using the Color PAGE Gel Rapid Preparation Kit, load 15 µL of each sample and 5 µL marker in the last well, electrophorese at 80 V then 140 V until the 25 kDa marker is about to exit, cut the gel to retain the 25–60 kDa region, immerse gel and filter papers in transfer buffer, cut PVDF membrane, wet in methanol, and transfer proteins onto PVDF at 21 V for 60 min using a Trans‑Blot SD system.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 10 % SDS‑PAGE gel (1.0 mm, 15 wells) per kit instructions.
Load 15 µL of each sample; load 5 µL protein marker in the final well.
Run electrophoresis at 80 V; increase to 140 V when proteins reach the resolving gel.
Stop when the 25 kDa marker is about to run out of the gel.
Excise gel portion spanning 25–60 kDa.
Immerse gel and thick filter papers in transfer buffer.
Cut PVDF membrane to size and soak in methanol.
Transfer proteins to PVDF at 21 V for 60 min using Trans‑Blot SD system.

steps.title: Block membrane and incubate antibodies
steps.instruction: Block the PVDF membrane in blocking buffer for 2 h on a horizontal shaker, incubate with anti‑phospho‑S175‑SnRK2s primary antibody (1:3000) in fresh blocking buffer for 12–14 h at 4 °C with gentle shaking, wash three times with TBST (10 min each), incubate with anti‑rabbit secondary antibody (1:5000) in fresh blocking buffer, and wash again three times with TBST (10 min each).

substeps.instruction: Block membrane in blocking buffer for 2 h (horizontal shaker).
Incubate with primary antibody (anti‑phospho‑S175‑SnRK2s, 1:3000) in fresh blocking buffer for 12–14 h at 4 °C with gentle shaking.
Wash membrane 3 × 10 min with TBST.
Incubate with secondary antibody (anti‑rabbit, 1:5000) in fresh blocking buffer.
Wash membrane 3 × 10 min with TBST.

steps.title: Prepare gel for in‑gel kinase assay
steps.instruction: Cast a 0.75 mm thick resolving gel (15 wells, 3.5 mL) and cover with ethanol; polymerize at 22 °C for 1 h, pour off ethanol, cast a 0.75 mm stacking gel (1.5 mL) with a 15‑well comb and polymerize another hour at 22 °C, assemble the gel in an electrophoresis tank with fresh running buffer, load 13 µL of each sample (reserve one well for 5 µL marker lacking kinases), run at 80 V then 120 V after ~30 min, stop when the 25 kDa marker reaches the gel bottom, retain the full resolving gel plus ~2 mm of stacking gel, and immerse the gel in SDS‑removal buffer to renature proteins before the kinase reaction.

substeps.instruction: Prepare resolving gel (0.75 mm, 15 wells, 3.5 mL).
Cover gel with ethanol; polymerize at 22 °C for 1 h.
Discard ethanol and prepare 0.75 mm stacking gel (1.5 mL) with 15‑well comb; polymerize at 22 °C for another 1 h.
Assemble gel in electrophoresis tank with fresh running buffer.
Load 13 µL of each sample; reserve one well for 5 µL protein marker (must lack protein kinases).
Run electrophoresis at 80 V; after ~30 min increase to 120 V once proteins enter separating gel.
Stop when the 25 kDa marker band reaches the bottom edge of the gel.
Retain the complete resolving gel and ~2 mm of stacking gel; avoid trimming.
Immerse gel in SDS‑removal buffer to remove SDS and renature proteins before the in‑gel kinase reaction.

description: SnRK2s are evolutionarily conserved core protein kinases controlling hyperosmotic stress and ABA signaling in plants.4 They are activated by the phytohormone ABA, and by hyperosmotic stresses triggered by multiple stimuli, including dehydration,1 cold,5 salinity, and high concentrations of mannitol, sorbitol, and other solutes (e.g., 300–800 mM).2,3 However, assessing SnRK2 activity via the classical in-gel kinase assay is challenging, limiting our understanding of osmotic stress sensing, SnRK2 activation, and signaling crosstalk with other stimuli. We generated the anti-phospho-S175-SnRK2s antibody, which recognizes the phosphorylation of SnRK2.6 (also named OST1 or SRK2E) at Ser175 and the phosphorylation of serine residues in the activation loop of multiple SnRK2s corresponding to Ser175 in SnRK2.6.3,6,7,8,9,10,11,12 The phosphorylation level of this conserved serine reflects SnRK2 activity. Therefore, immunoblotting with the anti-phospho-S175-SnRK2s antibody can be used as a substitute for the classical SnRK2 in-gel kinase assay, breaking down the barriers for studying SnRK2 activation and early osmotic stress signaling. SnRK2 activity can be further evaluated by detecting the phosphorylation of substrates (e.g., histones and ABF2 fragment) by SnRK2s via the in-gel kinase assays. The immunoblotting and in-gel kinase assays are suitable for evaluating endogenous SnRK2 activities in various mutants and transgenic lines.1,2 SnRK2s belong to a large family and are differentially activated by ABA and milder or severe osmotic stresses.3 Using transgenic lines, the band shift and immunoprecipitated kinase assays help us to assess the activity of specific members of SnRK2s, uncovering their unique regulatory mechanisms.3 The SnRK2.1pro:SnRK2.1-GFP and SnRK2.4pro:SnRK2.4-GFP transgenic lines in snrk2.1/4/5/7/8/9/10 mutant background, but not the overexpression lines, are suitable for band shift assays.3 These four methods will facilitate the evaluation of SnRK2 kinase ac
